checkpoints.title: CLI and ready package: aayu ready <feature> without --check, --guard, or --part is Approve to build. It is refused with exit 4 for an agent lane (a host marker, AAYU_AGENT=1 over MCP, or CI) before any write. For a person it checks the Initiative parent, Ready, the stories, each needed part approved with no drift, open review gaps, and the reviews (#876's critique.State through Options.CritiqueState, a test fake until #876 merges), and refuses with one line and the next command. It shows the effect (stories, baseline versions, budget, the changes of each version since the last approval, and the dismissals it ratifies) before GitHub's device code, reads everything again after it, and writes specs/<f>/approved.json only when both reads agree, on the ledger tip of the second read. Then Arjun posts the Feature's Ready snapshot and labels it status:ready. A story's Ready is unchanged
contracts: ready.Approval{Schema, Feature, Version, By, At, Presence, Baselines, Stories, Budget, Dismissals} at ready.ApprovalPath(f) = specs/<f>/approved.json
ready.Presence{Login, Via, Permission, ActionsRecord}: ActionsRecord is the hash of the presence.approve record in the actions log
ready.Critique{Reviews, In, AskedAt, Open, Dismissed}; ready.Dismissal{Finding, Reason, Words}
cli.Options.CritiqueState func(ctx, feature) (ready.Critique, error); nil means no review or finding is recorded
cli.ApproveReport{Repo, Feature, State approved|unchanged, Approval, LedgerPath, LedgerCommit, Ready, DryRun}
instrumentation: each approval is one ledger commit and one presence.approve record in the actions log; the Ready snapshot is a github.comment.ready-snapshot action
checkpoints.rollback: revert the PR; aayu ready <feature> labels the Feature Ready as the bot again, and approved.json records already on the ledger stay there unread
